parent_programme.relationship: Phase-VIII stochastic-observation successor; Phase-VII systematic-bias results remain immutable

scientific_question: When parameter assays have independent random full-support error rather than fixed systematic miscoding, how does repeated measurement change target distinguishability, and when does explicit assay-quality calibration reduce the repeat burden for the Phase-VII target-specific assay design?

fixed_ecological_design.scored_units: the same 67 W1 fibers with unresolved binary future target used in Phase VII
fixed_ecological_design.assay_fields: the lexicographically canonical assay fields from the Phase-VII complete deterministic action-library minimum for each fiber; the field set is recomputed from the frozen Phase-VII algorithm before stochastic scoring

error_kernel.rule: for a field with K frozen coordinate levels, observe the true code with p_correct and each of the K-1 other codes with probability (1-p_correct)/(K-1)
error_kernel.repeats: iid conditional on ecological world, field and global assay-quality world
error_kernel.global_quality_world: one of the two quality worlds applies to all selected assays and repeats

quality_calibration.effect_on_pairwise_affinity: joint hypotheses with different quality worlds become perfectly separated; same-quality pairs are unaffected

probabilistic_metric.name: worst target-discordant pair Bhattacharyya error upper bound
probabilistic_metric.independent_product: affinities multiply across fields and iid repeats
probabilistic_metric.pairwise_error_bound: equal-prior binary pairwise Bayes error is at most BC/2
probabilistic_metric.repeat_depths: integer n from 1 through 30; every selected Phase-VII assay field is observed n iid times
probabilistic_metric.important_boundary: this is a pairwise sufficient error bound, not a global posterior probability or a guarantee for one multiclass decision rule

exact_robust_boundary: because every stochastic categorical kernel has full support and every target-discordant ecological pair occurs under the same quality world, no finite repeat depth can create support-disjoint exact robust separation

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every scored target-unresolved fiber retains at least one same-quality target-discordant joint pair with overlapping full support at every finite repeat depth.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any finite-repeat exact support separation refutes H1 or exposes an implementation error.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one scored fiber has worst-pair BC/2 above 0.05 at n=1 and at or below 0.05 at some n<=30 using its frozen Phase-VII assay fields.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if no fiber crosses the threshold by repetition.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: For every scored fiber, the frozen Phase-VII assay fields plus assay-quality calibration reach worst-pair BC/2 <=0.05 by n<=30.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any fiber failing the threshold at n=30 refutes H3.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one scored fiber has a strictly lower total synthetic action count to reach the 0.05 bound when quality calibration is included.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if calibration never lowers total action count.

secondary_outputs: minimum repeat depth with and without quality calibration by transformation
total action-count distributions under both designs
fibers where no-calibration fails by n=30
S11 dormant-climate repeat depth and quality-calibration effect
worst-pair identity and whether the bottleneck is same-quality or cross-quality
stop_rules: Do not change p_correct values, 0.05 threshold, repeat cap or field domains after scoring.
Do not optimize a new assay field set after seeing stochastic results; use the frozen Phase-VII canonical fields.
Do not reinterpret BC/2 as an exact misclassification probability or global decision guarantee.
Do not call the symmetric categorical kernels calibrated real assay models.
Do not alter Phase-I through Phase-VII results.

novelty_boundary.candidate_contribution: An occurrence-conditioned BAM evidence-routing audit that explicitly separates exact finite-world robustness from risk-bounded repeated measurement for a prospectively frozen future ecological target.
